notes.title: We've redesigned the Campaign. Playtesters wanted for August 2025 playtest.
notes.content:
[p]Hi Reptorian Hunters,[/p][p][/p][p]Thanks to everyone that was involved in the latest playtest. The feedback has been great. People seem to be enjoying the combat section of the game. However, the campaign section of the game seemed to bog down the experience and pacing of the game. I had a similar feeling while playing myself. So, we've decided to redesign the campaign part of the game over the last couple of months.[/p][p][/p][p]Now, the campaign is from the perspective of your bridge, sitting in your captain's chair. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42509563/61839b74f0f62742e9e02f57a7f32d19b2ce253b.gif"][/img][/p][p]The primary goal is then same - to make it back to Earth (with a powerful enough ship to defeat the Reptorian mothership), and you still have to duck and hide from enemy ships and deal with interesting events on your way. But you do so via events that appear on the viewscreen and decisions you make via clicking on the in-game control panels. [/p][p][/p][p]I think it's looking pretty nice, even in its initial state. As always, big props to our talented illustrator for bringing this to life ([url="https://www.instagram.com/screwdycrow/"]https://www.instagram.com/screwdycrow/[/url]) ❤. [/p][p][/p][p]I think it feels a lot better, nipper and more natural to play now.[/p][p][/p][h1]August 2025 Playtest[/h1][p]Now that we've got a basic version of the new campaign working, we'd like to do another playtest to get some early feedback on it. [/p][p][/p][p]If you’ve already been on a Playtest, you don’t need to do anything, your existing Steam Key will continue to work and the game will automatically update in Steam. I’ll email you when I push the update.[/p][p][/p][p]If you haven’t already been on a Playtest, please sign up:[/p][p][/p][h2][b][url="https://mailchi.mp/8ccd2dbad62c/a8jrt08m14"]here[/url][/b]
[/h2][p]When the playtest starts, you’ll receive a Steam key to access the playtest. Feedback will be via a special channel in the [url="https://discord.gg/a7WD5GvX"]Discord[/url].[/p][p][/p][h1]Up Next[/h1][p]With this new campaign, I think the core gameplay loop is basically there. So the next developments will be about deepening and extending the game. New cards, new mechanics, more events in the campaign etc. [/p][p][/p][p]To make things a bit more interesting, we're thinking about having themed updates. The next one will be "Panic!", which will add a bunch of mechanics and cards around morale.[/p][p][/p][p]Until next time,[/p][h3]
James[/h3]

notes.title: Beam Her To The Sickbay!
notes.content:
[h1]Happy new year![/h1]
I've been keeping my head down working on Hunt of the Reptorians but I wanted to give an update on some of the things I've been working on. I’ve added loads of new things so I’ll only focus on some in this update.

[h1]Crew[/h1]
Crew now have a real presence on the ship, rather than being just animations as part of the room. Gunners are required to load the guns and the engineers can be moved to repair damaged parts of the ship. Crew can also be wounded so you will need to make sure they are protected (e.g. flipping your ship when they are making hull repairs) and can be sent to the sickbay to heal. You can, of course, damage enemy crew too and I'll be adding some weapon cards that are great for shredding Reptorians! 🔪🐊

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42509563/c208d52e733ea16ff39680b0611b7c64623ca927.gif[/img]

[h1]Your crew are your cards[/h1]
You may know from a previous update that each crew member contributes some cards to the overall deck. A big part of the game will revolve around improving these cards by upgrading your crew (and keeping them alive!)

Now, in battle, your crew's cards will only be in the deck if they are at their posts. For example, if your gunner gets hurt and needs to spend a while in the sickbay (also new), you won't be able to use any of their cards (like fire torpedoes) until they return.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42509563/2af9121492ba9e93a462d477a6308731daf8900b.gif[/img]

[h1]More…[/h1]
I'll go over some more things I've added in future updates. I might also do another video of me having a little play, which went down quite well last time I did it.

[h1]Plans for this year[/h1]
The game is starting to actually feel like a game now. I often find myself testing a new feature or fix and realise that I’d finished testing 10 minutes ago and I'm still playing! This is encouraging and probably time to get more feedback from play testing. I'm planning on creating a few play tests this year to ever-larger groups. I will, of course, keep you updated and let you know when this happens and how to get into a playtest.

Hope you all have a wonderful start to the year and looking forward to giving you more Reptorian updates soon.

James

notes.title: New Game Mechanic: Your Crew Are Your Cards. Plus New Card Designs 🎴
notes.content:
Hi Reptorian Hunters,

Sorry it’s been a little while since the last update. I’ve been adding lots of things trying to get something playable for upcoming playtests (keep posted for more details on these!). Things are going well and it’s starting to shape up quite nicely. At least the core gameplay loop.

[h2]Your crew are your cards[/h2]
One big change to the game mechanics is that your crew now have their own cards. But what does that mean? In most other deckbuilders, you have a global deck of cards that you add to, upgrade, and remove from your deck. My general philosophy for Hunt of the Reptorians is to make the cards an abstraction of captaining a ship. I didn’t feel that a global deck fitted well with that abstraction. So, I added crewmembers to the game. Behold!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42509563/69124bda9bf8b648b12e4bca979f4d6a9ce6fc51.jpg[/img]
Each crewmember contributes cards to the overall deck. As they gain experience, you can add more cards to them. You will also be able to upgrade or remove their existing cards.

At the moment, crewmembers don’t have a physical presence on the ship. I will be adding that later. However, once they do, you’ll have to make sure you protect and nurture them with training etc. It won’t be a good day when your highly experienced pilot is sucked out into space! 😨

[h2]New card designs and new illustrator![/h2]
You’ll also notice that I’ve updated the card design. I wanted to keep them clean and simple. In particular, I wanted to showcase the lovely illustrations by our new artist who has been wowing me with his gorgeous illustrations ([url=https://www.instagram.com/screwdycrow/]@screwdycrow[/url] if you were asking 😊). The illustrations now take up a lot more space to let them shine.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42509563/5fc0f5181cbf8987f6dce3b5037cc3709a1c1c2e.gif[/img]
Here is a little selection of cards in the game now:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42509563/9e3e07366538d47fe722d67799db4bd7eccfd72d.jpg[/img]
He also created the lovely crew portraits above. I’m hoping to show off more of his work soon.

See you in the next update.

James

notes.title: 🚀 Torpedoes incoming 😱 Evade! Evade! Evade! (dev log)
notes.content:
[h1]Projectiles and range (dev log)[/h1]

Hi again! I’ve been working hard on getting some new updates in to the combat system.  

[h2]Projectiles and the inter ship zone[/h2]

A core concept of the combat system is the idea of projectiles. Everything that is fired from a ship (railgun slugs, torpedoes, point defence, chaff, energy weapons, fighters etc.) is a projectile.

Projectiles that are fired from the ship must travel through the “inter ship zone” to reach their target. This is an area in between the ships the representing the journey projectiles take to reach their target.

Every turn, projectiles proceed across the inter ship zone. Some are fast and some are slow. When they reach the end of the inter ship zone, the surviving projectiles are unleashed on the target ship

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42509563/827e8fec78c429993291c431a8279725b767c114.gif[/img]

[h2]Range[/h2]

You can collect cards to increase and decrease range depending on whether your deck and the situation favours close or long range. 

For example, if the enemy is aggressively shooting down anything you fire at it, you can move to close range so that they don’t get a chance to shoot down your projectiles.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42509563/35d4abbba8b688a20f4118f1eb7b9514dbd5decc.png[/img]

[h2]Intercepting and evading projectiles[/h2]

Projectiles can be intercepted. You can intercept projectiles coming towards your ship with any projectile you like. However, some projectiles e.g. point defence are much better at shooting down projectiles than heavy railgun slugs.

You can also evade projectiles with certain cards. Some projectiles, like torpedoes are harder to evade than others, like basic slugs. Also, if you have a heavy ship with not enough engines, you will have a harder time evading incoming projectiles.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42509563/71aedfc12f3b58ab5fba5c2d4387433fbd503ccc.png[/img]

FYI - I’m working on some new card designs that I can hopefully show off soon. 

[h2]YouTube mini dev logs[/h2]

I’m starting to do little [url=https://www.youtube.com/@gibbonfiendstudios]mini dev logs on YouTube[/url]. Please subscribe if you want to get bite sized mini updates or just want to laugh at my terrible accents!

That’s all for this one. I look forward to giving you another update soon. Take care until then.

James

notes.title: Combat Mechanics: A High-Level Overview (Dev Log)
notes.content:
[h1]First dev log: overview of the combat system[/h1]

I'm very excited to start sharing what I've been working on for the last year or so - Hunt of the Reptorians.

It's a deck building game where you creatively smash spaceships apart from the outside in. In this first update, I'll give an overview of the combat system.

[h2]Build a deck to captain your ship[/h2]

I love deck building games. I also love managing spaceships. I felt the deck building model would work well as an abstraction of a ship's weapons and abilities and all the on board activities such as repairing, targeting, boarding, etc. It will also be really cool to experiment with crazy cards and synergies between them.

[h2]Dynamically carve up enemy ships... and avoid being carved up yourself[/h2]

I always loved making sand fortresses when I was a boy and loved the feeling I got when the fortress was surrounded with water and the waves started breaking up the fortress from the outside and my siblings and I scrambled to patch up the weaker bits until eventually the tide managed to find a way in! I wanted to capture a similar feeling in Hunt of the Reptorians. The safety of the internal rooms is protected by a layer of armour. Attacks generally break up this armour from the outside in until the juicy internal rooms are exposed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42509563/14908c80fa4081b91cf551d27c062cab7a3de44e.jpg[/img]

There is also the concept of external ship parts. These will include gun batteries, engines, shield bubble emitters etc. They are delicate external structures that can be easily damaged with well-targeted or lucky hits. They will need to be carefully protected by well-placed walls or shield bubbles.

Enemy ships come in all sorts of shapes and sizes. It's up to you to plan how you will dissect the ship and identify any vulnerable spots.

Would you like more detail?

That's all for this one. If you've read this far, I'm hoping you're interested. If so, please [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2003770/Hunt_of_the_Reptorians/]wishlist the game[/url]  If you want to be the first to get updates and get a place in early playtests, then please sign up to the [url=https://mailchi.mp/gibbonfiendstudios.com/n6ve6kui8p]mailing list[/url]. 

Till next time,

James
